html:
Johannes Vermeer was a painter in Delft, born in 1632, known for quiet scenes of women at home, lit by the light from a window.

Only about 35 paintings are known to be his, among them The Milkmaid, View of Delft and Girl with a Pearl Earring. He worked slowly, used costly blue pigment made from lapis lazuli, and may have used a camera obscura to study light. He died in debt in 1675, leaving eleven children.

He was little known after his death until a French critic rediscovered him in the 1860s. He is now one of the most admired painters of the Dutch Golden Age, beside Rembrandt. A Dutch forger fooled Nazi leaders with fake Vermeers in the 1940s. See the Netherlands and Leeuwenhoek, his Delft neighbour.
